## Picking delaySeconds

Choose based on the external event rather than Anthropic-specific prompt-cache windows. For untracked external CI/deploy checks use an appropriate 60–270s interval; for idle/quiet loops use 1200–1800s, or a 1200s+ fallback when tracked background work is running. Avoid short polling of harness-tracked tasks; they notify you automatically. The runtime clamps to [60, 3600].

## Avoid synchronized times when approximate

For approximate schedules, choose an off-minute (e.g., 8:57 instead of 9:00, 7 minutes past for hourly) to spread load. Honor exact user-requested clock times, including :00 or :30; never silently shift a specified time. The scheduler may add deterministic jitter.

## When to Use

Enter a worktree only if the user explicitly requested one or project CLAUDE.md/memory requires it. Creating/switching a branch or simply doing a coding task does not authorize a worktree: use the normal Git workflow unless expressly directed otherwise.

The canonical multi-stage pattern uses `export const meta = {name, description, phases: [...]}` followed by `pipeline(...)` and `agent(...)` calls, with independent `parallel(...)` verification of findings. Use the `workflow-authoring` skill for the precise API and full examples; do not invent function signatures.
